statement: A rebalance coordinator never creates a duplicate REPLACE for a partition whose earlier REPLACE it itself created moments ago just because the earlier operation's ledger INSERT has not become readable: in run-22 the coordinator's dedupe (which reads committed ledger rows) went blind while the ledger was write-starved, and 400ms after giving up on 25c9ce61's persist it minted duplicate ccff2762 for the same partition — the two then mutually blocked each other's source removal ('Quorum check failed: concurrent partition operation is active') at ~1s cadence for two minutes. The fix is a NARROW same-coordinator own-create memory: the coordinator remembers its own recent creates (partition, move shape, outcome-pending) and treats a not-yet-readable own create as in-flight for dedupe purposes, bounded by the operation's terminal outcome or a staleness horizon — NOT a blanket fail-closed admission when the ledger is unwritable (that would have blocked the healing corrective move ca191926 and is anti-convergent). Proven by a deterministic in-process test that delays ledger-row visibility after createOperation and asserts the planner's re-plan does not mint a duplicate (red on the current head), then by the standard suites.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

NARROW scope: same-coordinator own-create memory only. Blanket fail-closed admission when the ledger is unwritable is REFUTED as anti-convergent (it would have blocked the healing corrective move ca191926 in run-22). Bounded by terminal outcome or staleness horizon; must not fight the CL-008 dedupe layers (3 proven working) — this covers the window BEFORE the row is readable, which those layers cannot see. Evidence: run-22 duplicate ccff2762 minted 400ms after the same coordinator gave up persisting 25c9ce61.
